transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’ve been having some trouble with eating after work. Some evenings, especially if I’ve been trying to be really careful all day, I end up eating a lot more than I planned—dinner, then cereal or crackers, leftovers, sweets… all within a couple hours. It’s been bothering me.
Do you feel like you're in control of your eating during those evenings when you have a lot more than planned?
Yeah… I guess not really. Once I start, I keep going back to the kitchen, even when I’m telling myself I should stop. I don’t feel like I’m back in control until I’m already really full.
Do you feel guilty after these episodes of eating more than planned?
I don’t know… I feel bad about it, I guess. I try not to think about it too much afterward.
Do you ever try to make up for the extra food you ate by doing something to compensate, like exercising or vomiting?

Not vomiting, no. But… sometimes the next day I’ll skip breakfast and lunch, like I’m trying to make up for it. Or I’ll take a longer hike than usual, or push harder at softball conditioning even if I’m already tired.
How often do these episodes of eating more than planned happen?
Most weeks, I guess. Usually maybe one or two nights… for the past few months. Then the next day I’ll try to sort of balance it out, skipping meals or exercising longer.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Yeah… I guess I am. If my pants feel tight before, like, a client lunch or a leadership meeting, I start thinking I look sloppy… like people won’t take me seriously. I know that sounds a little much, but it gets in my head.
Do you ever have episodes where you eat a large amount of food in a short time and feel like you're not in control, without trying to make up for it the next day?

Yeah… I mean, on those nights, once I start, I’ll keep going back to the kitchen even when I’m telling myself to stop. I don’t really feel like I’m back in control until I’m already uncomfortably full.
How often do you skip meals or exercise more to make up for the extra food you ate?
Most weeks, I think. Usually after one of those nights… maybe once or twice a week, I’ll skip meals the next day or push myself to exercise longer. It’s been like that for a few months.
How often do you have episodes where you eat a lot more than planned and feel like you're not in control, without trying to make up for it the next day by skipping meals or exercising more?

Um… it’s been most weeks for the past few months. Usually like one or two nights where I eat way more than I meant to. But… I usually do try to make up for it the next day, like skipping meals or exercising longer.
How often do you have episodes where you eat a lot more than planned and feel like you're not in control, without doing anything to make up for it afterwards?
I mean… it’s usually most weeks, maybe one or two nights. But I don’t usually just leave it alone afterward—I tend to skip meals or exercise longer the next day.
On average, how many nights a week do you eat more than planned without trying to make up for it the next day?
I’m not really sure. I don’t keep track like that… and usually I do try to make up for it, so I don’t know what the average would be.
On a typical week, how many times do you eat a lot more than planned and feel like you're not in control, without doing anything to make up for it afterwards?
I… I don’t really know. Most of the time I do something after, so it’s hard to say how many times it happens without that. Maybe not many, but I haven’t counted.
How many days a week do you typically skip meals or exercise more to make up for eating more than planned?
Usually the day after… maybe one or two days a week. I’ll skip breakfast and lunch, or I’ll make myself do a longer hike or push harder at conditioning, even if I’m tired.
On average, how many times a week do you eat a lot more than planned and feel like you're not in control?
Most weeks… probably once or twice. Usually at night. I eat way more than I meant to, and it feels like I can’t really stop.
How often do you skip meals or exercise more as a way to make up for eating more than planned?
Usually the next day after one of those nights. I’ll skip breakfast and lunch, or I’ll make myself take a longer hike or push harder at softball conditioning… even if I’m tired.
How many times a week do you eat more than planned without trying to make up for it the next day?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think that happens very often… I guess I usually do something the next day, or at least think about it.
How often do you exercise more as a way to make up for eating more than planned?
Usually the next day, if I had one of those nights. I’ll tell myself I need to make up for it, so I might take an extra-long hike or push harder at softball conditioning… even if I’m tired.
How many days a week do you do something to make up for eating more than planned, like skipping meals or exercising more?
Maybe… a couple days a week? Usually it’s the day after one of those nights. I’ll skip breakfast and lunch or make myself do a longer hike, or push harder at conditioning, even if I’m worn out.
How often do you skip meals as a way to make up for eating more than planned?
I guess mostly the next day after one of those nights. I’ll skip breakfast and sometimes lunch… telling myself I’m making up for it. Not every day, but it happens.
How many times a week do you do something to make up for eating more than planned?
Most weeks… probably once or twice. Like, if I have a night where I really overdo it, the next day I’ll try to make up for it somehow.
